The claimants are in appeal challenging the liability fastened on the owner of one of the vehicles to pay 50% of the compensation and have sought for enhancement of compensation awarded by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (henceforth referred to as 'the Tribunal'), in MVC No.477/2013, vide judgment and award dated 16.06.2015.
2.
The claimants are the wife, son and mother of deceased Shamsheer Khan.

The records of the Tribunal disclose that the deceased and another person named Syed Shamsheer were proceeding to Ahmadabad as per the directions of the owner of lorry bearing registration No.KA.39/5406.
The deceased was sitting on the left side of the driver in the cabin and the vehicle was driven by Syed Shamsheer.

The driver drove the lorry in a rash and negligent manner, while another bus bearing registration No.MH-28/B-8495 (henceforth referred as 'offending NC: 2023:KHC-K:1451 vehicle')
was also driven in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against each other.

As a result,
Shamsheer Khan sustained injuries and died at the spot.

The claimants claimed that Shamsheer Khan was a driver and was earning a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month and therefore, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (henceforth referred as 'the MV Act,
1988'), claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle as well as the insurer of the lorry .
3. The claim petition was contested by the insurer of both the vehicles.
The owner of the offending vehicle contended that the driver of the lorry was negligent and was responsible for the accident.
4. However, the insurer of the lorry contended that the accident occurred in the middle of the road and therefore, negligence has to be attributed to both the drivers.
Consequently, liability had to be fastened on the drivers of both the vehicles.
It also contended that the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1451 lorry was brought for use on the road without a fitness certificate which was a breach of the terms and conditions of the policy of insurance.
Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
5. Claimant No.1 was examined as P.W.1 and she marked Exs.P.1 to P.9.

The insurer of the lorry was examined as R.W.1 and the insurance policy of both the vehicles were marked as Exs.R.1 and R.2.
6.

Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the claimants were unable to prove that the deceased was employed as a spare driver in the lorry and therefore, it held that the deceased was a gratuitous passenger travelling in the vehicle.
It also held that the accident occurred in the middle of the road and therefore, the drivers of both the vehicles were negligent and responsible for the accident.
In so far as the quantum of compensation to which the claimants were entitled to, it held that the deceased was 29 years old at the time of accident.

It considered the notional income of the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1451 deceased at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month and deducted 1/3rd towards his personal and living expenses and determined the following compensation:
1. Towards loss of Rs.8,16,000/-

3

2. Towards loss of Rs.10,000/-
consortium 3. Towards transportation of Rs.10,000/-
dead body and funeral expenses 4. Towards loss of love and Rs.10,000/-
affection 5. Towards loss of estate Rs.10,000/-
Total Rs.8,56,000/-
7.

In so far as the liability to pay compensation is concerned, it held that the owner of the lorry was liable to pay 50% of the compensation while the insurer of the offending vehicle was liable to pay the remaining 50% along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
Being aggrieved by NC: 2023:KHC-K:1451 the finding regarding negligence, liability and the quantum of compensation, the claimants are in appeal.

8. Learned counsel for the claimants contended that the claimants were entitled to pursue the claim against any one of the tortfeasors and it was for the Court to determine the liability of each tortfeasor, if all the tortfeasors were arrayed as parties in the claim petition.
Therefore, the Tribunal could have fastened the liability to pay the compensation on any one of the tortfeasors.
In this regard, he placed reliance on the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. And Others1.

entities.text: Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. And Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In so far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, learned counsel contends that the Tribunal must have assessed the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month and must have factored 40% of the notional income as the loss of future prospects since the deceased was 29 years old.

He further claimed that the claimants [2015] SCCR 526 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1451 were entitled to loss of consortium in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Versus Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others2 9.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Versus Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the insurer of the lorry contended that the deceased was travelling as a gratuitous passenger in the goods vehicle and therefore, the risk to such passenger was not covered and hence, insurer was not liable to pay compensation in view of Section 143(2)(b) and 147 (2)(b) of the MV Act, 1988.
Consequently, no liability could be fastened upon the insurer of the lorry.
He contended that the insurer cannot be directed to pay the compensation and recover it from the owner.

10. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer of the offending vehicle contends that the Tribunal has rightly attributed the negligence between the driver of the lorry and the driver of the offending Tarunnum W/O Shamsheer Khan And Ors vs Isamuddin S/O Syed Sab And Ors on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170173162/
4 vehicle and therefore, the (2018) 18 SCC 130 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1451 claimants were bound to proceed against the owner/insurer of the lorry.
11.

entities.text: Shamsheer Khan And Ors vs Isamuddin S/O Syed Sab And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the insurers as well as the learned counsel for the claimants.

12. As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the claimants, the claimants were entitled to pursue the claim against any of the tortfeasors and it is for the Tribunal to direct one of the tortfeasors to indemnify the claimants and permit that tortfeasor to recover the proportionate amount from other tortfeasor.
The claimants being third parties cannot be exposed to the risk of the proceeding against the owner of the lorry, who could dodge the payment of compensation.

The purpose of Section 166 of the MV Act, 1988, is to provide immediate and reasonable compensation to the dependents of the deceased and therefore, they cannot be driven into labyrinthine litigation.
In that view of the matter as rightly contended by the learned counsel for the claimants, the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1451 claimants are entitled to proceed against any one of the tortfeasors.
In the case on hand, the finding recorded by the Tribunal is that both the vehicles were involved in the accident and the deceased was travelling in the lorry bearing registration No.KA.39/5406.
The deceased was found to be a gratuitous passenger and therefore, there was no statutory cover to the risk of such gratuitous passenger.
There is no error in this finding as both the vehicles were heavy vehicles on the road and were involved in a head on collision.
Therefore, the owner of the lorry was liable to indemnify the claimants.

Be that as it may, now that all the tortfeasors are on record, this Court can direct any one of tortfeasors to pay the compensation determined and permit the complying tortfeasor to proceed against non-complying tortfeasor to recover the proportionate compensation in the same proceedings executing this judgment and award.

13. In that view of the matter, it is held that the claimants are entitled to proceed to recover the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1451 compensation and interest from the insurer of the offending vehicle, namely,
respondent Nos.3 and 4 herein.
The respondent Nos.3 and 4 may thereafter recover 50% of the compensation and interest paid from respondent No.1 by executing this judgment in accordance with law.

14. In so far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal committed an error in considering the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month while in similar circumstances, the notional income is considered at a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month.
The claimants are also entitled to loss of future prospects at the rate of 40%.

Consequently, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation which is re- determined as follows:-

. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.
The compensation of Rs.8,56,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.14,82,800/-.

The enhanced compensation with interest is payable by the owner/insurer of the offending vehicle/respondent Nos.3 and 4, who shall recover 50% of the compensation and interest so paid from the respondent No.1 in the same proceedings in accordance with law.

The respondent No.4 being the insurer of the offending vehicle shall deposit the entire compensation - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1451 with interest before the Tribunal within one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
After deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and accrued interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant No.1 in any Nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
